publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This research aims to explain the factors that influence consumer purchases on the Xiaohongshu platform, a popular social commerce platform in China. The study encompasses various aspects of this subject, including a basic platform overview, an exploration of consumer characteristics, a comprehensive analysis of influencing factors, and the final impact of these factors on the purchasing behavior of Xiaohongshu users. This research endeavors to contribute to the understanding of consumer behavior on Xiaohongshu, with a specific focus on how various factors shape purchasing decisions. The resulting knowledge and guidelines will be invaluable for Thai businesses aiming to establish a foothold and thrive in the dynamic and rapidly growing market of Xiaohongshu.

articleTitle: Identifying Key Factors Affecting Purchase Intentions Toward Electric Vehicles in Thailand
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: This paper conducts a Systematic Literature Review to explore the key factors influencing consumer intentions to purchase Electric Vehicles in Thailand. The study underpinned by the SLR methodology adapted from the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) framework. We examine 36 related articles via Rayyan software to identify publication trends, methodologies, theories, and variables factors in existing research to EVs purchase intentions. The analysis result reveals that consumer attitudes, societal norms, perceived behavioral control, and environmental concerns are pivotal in shaping EVs purchase intentions. The study uncovers research gaps, particularly in the areas of habitual behavior and hedonic motivation, suggesting the need for further exploration. Our study contributes to the discourse on sustainable transportation by offering insights that can inform targeted marketing strategies, and infrastructural planning in Thailand.

articleTitle: Social Networks and Knowledge Transfer in Real Estate Business in Chiang Mai
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: Driven by China’s One Belt, One Road initiative, the real estate market in Thailand has attracted much attention from Chinese investors. As intangible knowledge with added value is an important resource in the knowledge economy, real estate agents with this kind of knowledge play an important intermediary role in the real estate market. They use their information advantage to bridge the information gap between potential buyers and sellers in the local real estate market, reduce search costs and improve the match between buyers and sellers. At the same time, knowledge is also transferred among the real estate agents themselves. While sharing knowledge with competitors may seem counter-intuitive, it is important to share knowledge in a market where competitors are each other’s stakeholders. It enables them to have more success with their real estate transactions and help to increase the closing rates in the market as a whole. Therefore, the purpose of this research is to identify the process by which real estate agents in Chiang Mai transfer knowledge and the factors that influence them to do so by conducting social network analysis to develop a framework for real estate businesses in Chiang Mai to transfer knowledge. This study adopts a mixed research approach, first using social network analysis (SNA) as a quantitative research tool, then conducting open-ended question interviews with experts and key actors as a qualitative research, and finally conducting interviews through the SECI model to design a knowledge transfer framework.

articleTitle: Development of Science Virtual Reality Lab Simulation (SVLS): Enhancing Immersive Experiences
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: In order to improve student learning in primary science laboratories, this pilot study explores the development and application of a Virtual Reality (VR) simulation system called Science Virtual Lab Simulation (SVLS). Unlike traditional teaching approaches, SVLS is designed to provide an engaging and interactive environment that helps young learners better understand scientific concepts. Three crucial components of virtual reality (VR) in education are highlighted by the study’s methodology: the system’s overall usability, the interaction between users and VR technology, and the learning experience itself. The results showed students’ desire and enthusiasm to learn were increased by the VR environment, which made scientific concepts easier to understand. The study suggested that the active use of VR technology may contribute to enhancing science education by potentially making learning more engaging and enjoyable. The user-friendliness and intuitiveness of the VR system appeared to play a role in its effective integration into learning environments. Additionally, the research highlighted the importance of designing VR systems with interfaces and instructions that are considerate of the cognitive and physical abilities of young students, though further studies are recommended to fully understand these impacts. To summarize, the SVLS prototype showcases how VR may revolutionize the teaching of primary science. It highlights how well built VR systems can greatly enhance various elements of education, including learning engagement, technological interaction, and overall academic outcomes.

articleTitle: Designing Interactive Mobile Application to Create Online-Learning Experience of the Future
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Conference on Digital Arts, Media and Technology with ECTI Northern Section Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (ECTI DAMT & NCON)
abstract: Lifestyle in the globalization era like today has been tremendously changed from what it was in the past. This technological evolution has increasingly facilitated human-computer interactions, enabling technologies to adapt and cater to individual requirements across various domains, including education. Personalized-Learning is a learning model that is being explored and studied widely as it offers flexibility to lifestyle, living, travelling, and learning characteristics. It can be said that personalized-learning is a learning model in response to today needs and future needs. The present study introduces the Personalized Learning Online Environment (PLOEN), an innovative online platform designed to redefine learning from a contemporary to a futuristic perspective through a tri-dimensional approach. The first dimension of PLOEN is rooted in the OECD Learning Framework 2030, focusing on the holistic development of knowledge, skills, attitudes, and values. This is achieved through a pedagogical process that involves reflection, anticipation, and action, thereby fostering essential competencies for global participation. The second dimension incorporates the concept of gamification in the educational process. This is operationalized through elements such as Point (Level), Badge, and Leaderboard (User Competencies Dashboard) within the application, which collectively cultivate a ‘joyful’ learning environment, subtly blending education with gaming elements. The third dimension represents a novel human-computer interaction model, engaging all five senses to connect users with the system. This involves the integration of Neuron, Touch, Sound, Movement, and Voice-User Interfaces, which interact with various sensors like mobile, gesture, and face-detection technologies. The research results can be applied to personalized learning to create a dimension of learning and interaction in the future by expanding the scope of digital aesthetics that does not require only the use of fingertip sensory nerve endings and the separation between the digital world and the real world. Furthermore, the research proposed that the research on interactive technologies in education is important and it is worthwhile to study related issues further in the future.
